help: Render a 3D model (GLB) into sprite frames from the camera of a game, with Blender.
um render3d model.glb out/ --preset iso8 --canvas 256x256 --length 150 --engine eevee
Rendering from 3D keeps every facing and frame consistent, which per-frame image generation cannot do.
Typical flow: concept art, `um fal model3d` (image to 3D), these renders, then the sprite format of the engine.
aoe2      ortho 30 deg, 16 headings clockwise from east (AoE2 DE and Genie unit order)
iso8      ortho 30 deg (2:1 diamond tiles), 8 headings clockwise from east
topdown   ortho 90 deg, 8 headings (twin-stick and top-down shooters)
side      ortho 0 deg, 2 headings: facing right, facing left (platformers, Terraria style)
turntable persp 20 deg, 24 headings (icons, previews, promo spins)
Blender must be on PATH, or set BLENDER=/path/to/blender.
Pack them with `um sprite sheet`, or with a writer for the engine.

messages.notFound: Blender not found: install it (blender.org, or `snap install blender --classic`) or set BLENDER=/path/to/blender

preset.help: aoe2, iso8, trueiso, topdown, side, or turntable (default aoe2)

canvas.help: frame size px: N or WxH

length.help: longest horizontal side of the model (or height with --measure height) in px

forward-yaw.help: degrees to turn the model so that its front faces +X (east)

ground-y.help: px from the top where the ground point goes (default: canvas center)
